mainTopic: אביי and רבא on unavoidable but intended benefit (לא אפשר ומתכוין), and a side discussion of when sound, sight, smell, and finished-מצוה items are subject to מעילה.
overview: אביי and רבא argue about a benefit that cannot be avoided when the person intends to enjoy it (לא אפשר ומתכוין). אביי permits it and רבא forbids it. רבא explains that רבי יהודה's rule about intent only works to make things stricter. אביי brings proof from רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, who taught in the shade of the היכל, but רבא answers that the היכל was built for its inside, so its shade was never forbidden. רבא's own proofs are also pushed aside: the workers lowered in boxes into the בית קדשי הקדשים were only a special מעלה, and בר קפרא's teaching can refer to people standing outside. The גמרא then examines בר קפרא's rule that sound, sight, and smell are not מעילה, and רב פפא corrects it: smell is free of מעילה only after the smoke rises, once the מצוה is done. That principle is tested against תרומת הדשן, and the גמרא explains that it and בגדי כהונה (or עגלה ערופה) are exceptions that teach no general rule. Finally, the גמרא returns to אביי and רבא with a heifer that threshed grain, and challenges the answer that its verse disqualifies any work at all.

steps.title: רבא: רבי יהודה's rule only works for stringency
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רבי יהודה's rule, treating אין מתכוין like מתכוין, only makes things stricter. It cannot be flipped to treat a person who intends as if he did not intend in order to be lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא would say to you: רבי יהודה only said that someone without intent is treated like someone with intent in order to be strict. But to treat someone who does intend as if he had no intent, so that we can be lenient, he never said that.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his position by limiting how far רבי יהודה's rule goes. He says it only works in one direction, toward stringency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that even without intent, a forbidden act still counts, which makes him strict. רבא says you cannot turn this around and say that when there is no other choice, a person's intent should be ignored to permit the act. So nothing in רבי יהודה's view supports permitting לא אפשר ומתכוין.

keyTerms.meaning: intends; the person wants the forbidden benefit or result
one who does not intend it
to be strict
to be lenient
he only said this up to here, meaning only in this case

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read רבי יהודה's rule as a two-way equation. רבא's whole point is that it only works one way: lacking intent can make you liable, but having intent can never be cancelled to permit something.

phrases.english: And Rava would say to you:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda only said
that one who does not intend is like one who intends
only to be strict;
but that one who intends is like one who does not intend
in order to be lenient, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא אָמַר לָךְ: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier attempt on the daf to tie the אביי and רבא dispute to the views of תנאים. Here רבא explains why רבי יהודה does not support permitting the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a תנא's principle (it only works toward stringency)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think רבי יהודה's equation of intent and non-intent could also be used to be lenient, permitting לא אפשר ומתכוין.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה's rule only works לחומרא, so it gives no support for permitting a case where the person intends.

steps.title: אביי's proof: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי teaching in the shade of the היכל
steps.stepSummary: אביי proves that לא אפשר ומתכוין is permitted. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי sat in the shade of the היכל teaching all day. He had no other choice, he surely enjoyed the shade, and yet it was allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: How do I know my view? It was taught in a ברייתא: they said about רבן יוחנן בן זכאי that he would sit in the shade of the היכל and teach all day long. Isn't this a case where there was no other option, and he intended to enjoy the shade, and still it was permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a ברייתא to prove his side, that unavoidable benefit is permitted even when the person intends to enjoy it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Benefiting from הקדש is normally forbidden. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי needed a big place for his crowd, so it was לא אפשר, and he clearly wanted the shade, so it was מתכוין. Because he still did it, אביי concludes that this combination is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do I say it? (introduces a proof)
as it was taught in a ברייתא
the shade of the היכל
it is impossible to avoid
and it is permitted

phrases.english: Abaye said: From where do I say it?
As it was taught: They said about him,
about Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai,
that he would sit in the shade of the Sanctuary
and expound the entire day.
And here, isn't it impossible to avoid, and he intends,
phrases.notes: There was no other place large enough for the crowd, and he surely enjoyed the shade.

phrases.english: and yet it is permitted?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ — דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the רבי יהודה discussion. אביי now brings direct proof for his own view from a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's ruling that לא אפשר ומתכוין is permitted
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about רבן יוחנן בן זכאי teaching all day in the shade of the היכל

steps.title: רבא: The Sanctuary was built for its inside
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects אביי's proof. The היכל was built for its interior space, so the shade outside it was never forbidden in the first place.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: The היכל is different, because it was made for its inside.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes away אביי's proof by showing that the case of the shade is not really forbidden benefit at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition of benefiting from the היכל applies to what it was built for, which is its inner space. Shade falling outside the building is not part of that, so it is fully permitted. That means the story says nothing about לא אפשר ומתכוין.

keyTerms.meaning: it is different
the Sanctuary building in the בית המקדש
which was made for its interior

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying unavoidable intended benefit is fine here. He is saying there was no forbidden benefit at all, so the case cannot serve as a proof either way.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
The Sanctuary is different, for it was made for its interior.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא אָמַר: שָׁאנֵי הֵיכָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly rejects אביי's proof in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof completely by showing the case is not one of forbidden benefit.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The shade outside the היכל was never forbidden, because the building's sanctity concerns its interior use.

steps.title: רבא's proof: Workers lowered in boxes into the בית קדשי הקדשים
steps.stepSummary: רבא proves his view, that לא אפשר ומתכוין is forbidden. When workers had to repair the בית קדשי הקדשים, they were lowered in boxes so they could not enjoy looking at it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: How do I know my view? It was taught: there were openings in the upper floor of the בית קדשי הקדשים. Through them they lowered the workers in boxes, so that their eyes would not enjoy looking at the בית קדשי הקדשים. Isn't this a case where it was impossible to avoid, and they would intend to enjoy it, and it is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings his own ברייתא to prove that unavoidable benefit is forbidden when the person intends to enjoy it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The repairs had to be done, so entering was לא אפשר. The workers would likely enjoy the sight, which is מתכוין. Because the חכמים went out of their way to block the view with boxes, רבא concludes that this combination is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: openings or hatches
the upper floor above the בית קדשי הקדשים
they lower down
craftsmen, workers
their eyes feast on it, enjoy looking
and it is forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: אביי permits לא אפשר ומתכוין, based on the shade of the היכל. רבא rejects that proof because the היכל was built for its interior. רבא forbids it, citing the workers lowered in boxes into the בית קדשי הקדשים, though the next step rejects this proof.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the basic rule for benefit that comes to a person against his will, a topic that applies all over הלכה, for example hearing music or smelling a forbidden scent.

phrases.english: Rava said: From where do I say it?
As it was taught: There were openings
in the upper floor of the Holy of Holies,
through which they would lower the craftsmen in boxes,
so that their eyes would not feast
on the Holy of Holies.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא הָכָא דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר וְקָא מִיכַּוֵּין —
phrases.english: And here, isn't it impossible to avoid, and they would intend,
phrases.notes: The repairs had to be done, and the workers would enjoy the sight.

phrases.english: and it is forbidden?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ, דְּתַנְיָא לוּלִין הָיוּ פְּתוּחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting אביי's proof, רבא brings his own proof for the opposite view.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that לא אפשר ומתכוין is forbidden
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about craftsmen lowered in boxes into the בית קדשי הקדשים so they would not gaze at it

steps.title: The boxes were only an extra honor, not proof of a prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבא's proof from the boxes. Seeing holy things is not מעילה at all, so lowering the workers in boxes was only a special stringency for the בית קדשי הקדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really understand it that way? But רבי שמעון בן פזי said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי, who said it in the name of בר קפרא: sound, sight, and smell are not subject to מעילה! Rather, the boxes were an extra stringency made especially for the בית קדשי הקדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא's proof from the workers in boxes. It shows that this case cannot teach us a general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא assumed the boxes were used because enjoying the sight would be forbidden. The גמרא answers that looking at holy things is never מעילה, since sight is not a physical use. So the boxes were only an added layer of honor (מעלה) unique to the holiest place, and nothing can be learned from them about לא אפשר ומתכוין in general.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And can you understand it so?!' An expression that rejects the reasoning just given
The prohibition of misusing or benefiting from property that belongs to the בית המקדש
Sound, sight, and smell: kinds of benefit that are not physical
An extra stringency or added honor that the חכמים established

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the boxes prove that looking at the בית קדשי הקדשים is מעילה. The גמרא's point is the opposite: sight is not מעילה at all, and the boxes were only a special extra honor.

phrases.english: And can you understand it that way?!
But didn't Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi say
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said
in the name of Bar Kappara:
Sound, sight, and smell
phrases.notes: The sound of the music in the בית המקדש, and the sight and smell of the קטורת

phrases.english: are not subject to the prohibition of misusing holy property!
Rather, they made an extra stringency
for the Holy of Holies.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִסְבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's proof from step 4
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the boxes. It does not disprove רבא's position itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The boxes were not needed because of a real prohibition. Sight is not מעילה, so the boxes were only a special מעלה unique to the בית קדשי הקדשים.

steps.title: Another version: רבא proves his view from בר קפרא's teaching
steps.stepSummary: According to another version, רבא's proof comes from בר קפרא. Sound, sight, and smell are not מעילה, but they are still forbidden. This must refer to people standing inside, who cannot avoid it, so לא אפשר ומתכוין is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it differently. רבא said: From where do I know my view? As it was taught: רבי שמעון בן פזי said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי, who said it in the name of בר קפרא: sound, sight, and smell are not subject to מעילה. This means there is no מעילה, but there is still a prohibition. Is this not talking about people standing inside, who cannot avoid it, and who intend to enjoy it? And it is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רבא's proof. Here his source is בר קפרא's teaching rather than the workers in boxes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads בר קפרא carefully. Saying there is no מעילה implies that a lesser prohibition (איסורא) still exists. He then argues that this prohibition must apply to people inside the מקדש, who cannot avoid hearing, seeing, and smelling. That would prove that לא אפשר ומתכוין is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Some say': introduces another version of the discussion
'From where do I say this?' The speaker is about to bring a source for his own view
A prohibition, here a lesser one that is not מעילה
'Is it not...?' Proposes a reading of a source in order to prove a point
It is impossible to avoid, and he intends to benefit

phrases.english: Some say:
Rava said: From where do I say this?
As it was taught:
Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said
in the name of Bar Kappara:
Sound, sight, and smell
are not subject to the prohibition of misusing holy property.
It is misuse of holy property that does not apply,
but a prohibition does apply.
phrases.notes: A rabbinic prohibition

phrases.english: Is it not referring to those standing inside,
where it is impossible to avoid, and he intends to benefit,
and yet it is forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רָבָא: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second version of רבא's proof, replacing the rejected proof from the boxes
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that לא אפשר ומתכוין is forbidden
steps.raayaSupportSource: בר קפרא's teaching, read as implying that a prohibition exists even without מעילה, applied to those inside the מקדש

steps.title: No, it refers to people standing outside
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. בר קפרא's prohibition could refer to people standing outside, who could avoid it. That is a case of אפשר ומתכוין, which everyone agrees is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is talking about people standing outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רבא's proof by reading בר קפרא's teaching as being about a different group of people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People standing outside the מקדש have no reason to be there, so they could easily avoid the sound, sight, and smell. That makes it a case of אפשר ומתכוין, which is forbidden according to everyone. So the source says nothing about the disputed case of people inside who have no choice.

keyTerms.meaning: Those standing outside, who are not required to be there
Possible: the person could have avoided the situation

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions, רבא's proofs are pushed aside. The boxes were only a special מעלה, and בר קפרא's prohibition can be read as applying to people outside, who could avoid the benefit.

phrases.english: No, it refers to those standing outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, לְאוֹתָן הָעוֹמְדִין בַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the reading that applies the prohibition to people inside
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The prohibition can refer to people outside, a case of אפשר ומתכוין, which all agree is forbidden. So it proves nothing about לא אפשר ומתכוין.

steps.title: Returning to בר קפרא's teaching itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now examines בר קפרא's teaching on its own terms: sound, sight, and smell are not subject to מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now back to the teaching itself. רבי שמעון בן פזי said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי, who said it in the name of בר קפרא: sound, sight, and smell are not subject to מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא restates בר קפרא's teaching so it can analyze it directly. This step is setting up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, the teaching was used only as a tool in the אביי and רבא debate. Now the גמרא turns to the teaching itself, to check whether it fits with other sources.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': the גמרא returns to examine a teaching that was quoted earlier

phrases.english: Returning to the matter itself.
Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said
in the name of Bar Kappara:
Sound, sight, and smell
are not subject to the prohibition of misusing holy property.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אביי and רבא debate and returns to analyze the quoted teaching itself
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Non-physical benefit, meaning sound, sight, and smell, is not subject to מעילה

steps.title: But a ברייתא says smelling the incense is מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges בר קפרא. A ברייתא says that one who smells the קטורת is exempt from punishment but has committed מעילה. That suggests smell can be מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is smell really not subject to מעילה? But it was taught: one who mixes the קטורת in order to learn how, or in order to hand it over to the community, is exempt. One who mixes it in order to smell it is liable. And one who smells it is exempt, except that he has committed מעילה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the part of בר קפרא's teaching that says smell is not מעילה, using a ברייתא that says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא separates three cases. Mixing the קטורת to learn or to give it to the ציבור is exempt. Mixing it in order to enjoy its smell brings punishment, based on the פסוק. Just smelling it brings no punishment, yet the ברייתא says the person has still committed מעילה, which directly contradicts בר קפרא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But it was taught': introduces a ברייתא that contradicts what was just said
One who mixes or compounds spices
The incense offered in the בית המקדש
Exempt from punishment
Liable to punishment
He committed מעילה, misusing holy property

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two different actions. 'מפטם להריח', making the incense in order to smell it, brings punishment. 'המריח', just smelling it, brings no punishment but is still called מעילה, and that is the point that challenges בר קפרא.

phrases.english: And is smell not subject to misusing holy property?
But it was taught in a baraita:
One who mixes the incense
in order to teach himself how,
or in order to hand it over to the community
is exempt.
If he made it in order to smell it, he is liable.
phrases.notes: Based on the פסוק in שמות ל:לח

phrases.english: And one who smells it is exempt,
except that he has misused holy property!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרֵיחַ אֵין בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם מְעִילָה? וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the teaching restated in step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: בר קפרא's claim that smell is not subject to מעילה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly says that one who smells the קטורת has committed מעילה. That contradicts the claim that smell is never מעילה.

steps.title: רב פפא restates the rule: smell is exempt only after the smoke rises
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers the challenge. Sound and sight are not מעילה because they have no substance. Smell is not מעילה only after the column of smoke rises, since the מצוה is already done.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: Sound and sight are not subject to מעילה, because they have no substance. And smell, after its column of smoke has risen, is not subject to מעילה, since its מצוה has already been done.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the ברייתא about the קטורת by giving a corrected version of the rule in רב פפא's name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said that smelling the קטורת is מעילה. רב פפא agrees, but only for the early stage, before the smoke rises, when the smell is still part of the מצוה. Once the column of smoke has risen, the מצוה is finished, so smelling it then is no longer מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Misusing or benefiting from holy (הקדש) property
Physical substance
Its column of smoke
Its מצוה has already been done

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא does NOT say that smell is never מעילה. He divides smell into two stages. Before the smoke rises, smell can be מעילה, and that is the case the ברייתא discussed. After the smoke rises, it is not מעילה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This step brings in a new idea: once an item's מצוה is finished, it may lose its מעילה status. The rest of this passage tests that idea.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said:
phrases.notes: "Rather" signals that this replaces בר קפרא's version of the rule.

phrases.aramaic: קוֹל וּמַרְאֶה אֵין בָּהֶן מִשּׁוּם מְעִילָה,
phrases.english: Sound and sight are not subject to misuse of consecrated property,
because they have no substance.
And smell, after its column of smoke has risen —
phrases.notes: Smell is now limited to the later stage only.

phrases.english: is not subject to misuse of consecrated property,
since its מצוה has already been performed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9 by changing the wording of the rule about smell.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewording of the rule (אלא), splitting smell into two time stages
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Smell is never subject to מעילה, which conflicts with the ברייתא about the קטורת.
steps.terutzMaskana: Smell is מעילה before the smoke rises and not מעילה after, because by then the מצוה is done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sound and sight have no substance, so they are never מעילה. Smell is exempt only after the מצוה is finished.

steps.title: Challenge: the altar ashes stay forbidden even after their מצוה is done
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether every item whose מצוה is done loses מעילה. תרומת הדשן is done with its מצוה and is still forbidden for benefit, as the word ושמו teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that wherever an item's מצוה is done, it is not subject to מעילה? But תרומת הדשן has its מצוה done and is still subject to מעילה. As it is written, "and he shall put it beside the altar." This teaches that he should not scatter it. And "he shall put it" also teaches that one may not benefit from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reason רב פפא gave. It brings a case where the מצוה is finished but מעילה still applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's reason sounds like a general rule: once the מצוה is done, there is no more מעילה. But the ashes removed from the altar (תרומת הדשן) have already finished their מצוה. Even so, the תורה's word ושמו forbids any benefit from them. So the general rule seems to be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (a phrase that opens a challenge)
The daily removal of a portion of ashes from the altar
And he shall put it
That he should not scatter it
That one may not benefit from it

phrases.english: Is that to say that wherever its מצוה has been performed
it is not subject to misuse of consecrated property?!
But there is the removal of the ashes, whose מצוה has been performed —
and it is subject to misuse of consecrated property.
As it is written: "And he shall put it beside the altar" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא ו:ג

phrases.english: teaching that he should not scatter it,
"And he shall put it" — teaching that one may not benefit from it.
phrases.notes: The same word is read a second time to teach a ban on benefit.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּכֹל הֵיכָא דְּנַעֲשֵׂית מִצְוָתוֹ אֵין בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם מְעִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason (הואיל ונעשית מצותו) that רב פפא gave in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's principle that an item whose מצוה is done is no longer subject to מעילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A counterexample: תרומת הדשן has finished its מצוה, yet the תורה still forbids benefit from it.

steps.title: Answer: two verses teaching the same thing cannot set a general rule
steps.stepSummary: תרומת הדשן and בגדי כהונה are שני כתובין הבאין כאחד. Two verses that teach the same law are exceptions and cannot teach a general rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because תרומת הדשן and בגדי כהונה are two verses that come as one, and any two verses that come as one do not teach a general rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב פפא's rule. It explains that the ashes are a special exception and do not disprove the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה had to write the ban on benefit after the מצוה twice: once for the ashes and once for the כהן גדול's garments. If it were a general rule, one verse would have been enough. Writing it twice shows these two cases are exceptions. Everywhere else, the normal rule holds, and a finished מצוה means no מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Two verses that teach the same law
They do not teach a general rule for other cases
The priestly garments (here, the כהן גדול's linen garments of יום כיפור)

steps.confusionAlert: It might seem that two verses should make a law stronger. Here the logic works the other way. Because the תורה had to say the law twice, these cases are treated as exceptions, not as a model for other cases.
steps.whyThisMatters: שני כתובין הבאין כאחד אין מלמדין is a basic rule of Torah interpretation that appears throughout ש״ס.

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָווּ תְּרוּמַת הַדֶּשֶׁן וּבִגְדֵי כְהוּנָּה
phrases.english: Because the removal of the ashes and the priestly garments are
two verses that come as one,
and any two verses that come as one
do not teach a general rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָווּ תְּרוּמַת הַדֶּשֶׁן וּבִגְדֵי כְהוּנָּה שְׁנֵי כְתוּבִין הַבָּאִין כְּאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11 by showing that תרומת הדשן is an exception.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the counterexample to an exception (שני כתובין הבאין כאחד)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: תרומת הדשן shows that a finished מצוה does not remove מעילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: תרומת הדשן and בגדי כהונה are two exceptions that cannot be applied elsewhere, so רב פפא's general rule stands.

steps.title: Identifying the two verses: ashes and priestly garments
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא names the source for each of the two verses. For תרומת הדשן, it is ושמו, already quoted. For בגדי כהונה, it is והניחם שם, which teaches that the garments require burial.
steps.simpleTranslation: תרומת הדשן is what we already said. For בגדי כהונה, it is written, "and he shall leave them there." This teaches that they require burial (גניזה).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer by pointing to the verse for each of the two exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse for the ashes (ושמו) was already quoted in step 11. The new part is the verse for the כהן גדול's יום כיפור garments (והניחם שם). It teaches that once the service is done, the garments must be put away (buried) and may not be used. That confirms the second verse that teaches the same law, which completes the pair needed for the answer in step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: That which we already said
And he shall leave them there
Burial or storage that removes an item from any use

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא: once a holy item's מצוה is done, it is generally no longer subject to מעילה. Smell of the קטורת after the smoke rises is one example. תרומת הדשן and בגדי כהונה are offered as the two exceptions (שני כתובין הבאין כאחד), but the next step challenges this pairing according to רבי דוסא.

phrases.english: The removal of the ashes — that which we already said.
The priestly garments, as it is written: "And he shall leave them there" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא טז:כג

phrases.english: teaches that they require burial.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּרוּמַת הַדֶּשֶׁן הָא דַּאֲמַרַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the verse for each of the two cases named in step 12's answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both the altar ashes (ושמו) and the כהן גדול's יום כיפור garments (והניחם שם) stay forbidden for benefit after their מצוה is done.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The two exceptions are confirmed by their verses, so רב פפא's general rule stays in place.

steps.title: The answer fails according to רבי דוסא
steps.stepSummary: The pairing of תרומת הדשן with בגדי כהונה works for the רבנן. It does not work for רבי דוסא, who says the garments may still be used by a regular כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the רבנן, who say the verse teaches that the garments must be buried. But רבי דוסא disagrees with them. He says the garments are still fit for a regular כהן, and that 'he shall leave them there' only means the כהן גדול may not use them on another יום כפור. According to him, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 12. According to רבי דוסא, the בגדי כהונה are not forbidden after use, so they cannot be the second verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 needed two verses so that neither one could teach a general rule. According to רבי דוסא, the garments may still be worn by a regular כהן, so the only verse left is תרומת הדשן. A single verse CAN teach a general rule, so the problem from Step 11 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well (for this opinion, but not for another)
Burial or storing away of holy items
A תנא who disagrees with the רבנן about the יום כפור garments
A regular כהן, not the כהן גדול

steps.confusionAlert: רבי דוסא does not say the garments have no special status. He only says the restriction is narrower: the כהן גדול cannot reuse them on another יום כפור, but a regular כהן may wear them.

phrases.english: It works out well according to the Rabbis, who say
it teaches that they require burial
but according to Rabbi Dosa, who disagrees with them

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: אֲבָל רְאוּיִין הֵן לְכֹהֵן הֶדְיוֹט
phrases.english: who says: but they are fit for a common priest
phrases.notes: They are only disqualified for the כהן גדול on יום כפור.

phrases.english: and what is the meaning of 'and he shall leave them there'?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהֶם בְּיוֹם כִּפּוּרִים אַחֵר
phrases.english: that he may not use them on another Yom Kippur
what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְרַבָּנַן דְּאָמְרִי מְלַמֵּד שֶׁטְּעוּנִין גְּנִיזָה, אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי דּוֹסָא דִּפְלִיג עֲלַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer from Step 12, using the source from Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that תרומת הדשן and בגדי כהונה are two verses that teach the same law
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבי דוסא, the garments are not forbidden for all use after the מצוה. That leaves תרומת הדשן as a single verse, which could teach a general rule.

steps.title: Pairing the ashes with the heifer instead
steps.stepSummary: The second verse is עגלה ערופה, not בגדי כהונה. Together with תרומת הדשן, they are two verses that teach the same law and so do not teach a general rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because תרומת הדשן and עגלה ערופה are two verses that teach the same law, and any two verses that teach the same law do not teach a general rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by swapping in a different second example. The עגלה ערופה is also forbidden for benefit after its מצוה is done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even for רבי דוסא, the עגלה ערופה stays forbidden after its neck is broken. So there are still two verses with the same unusual law. Two such verses are treated as exceptions and cannot become a general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The heifer whose neck is broken for an unsolved murder
The daily removal of ashes from the מזבח
Two verses that teach the same law
They do not teach a general rule

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָווּ תְּרוּמַת הַדֶּשֶׁן וְעֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה
phrases.english: Because the removal of ashes and the heifer whose neck is broken
are two verses that come as one
and any two verses that come as one
do not teach a general principle

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָווּ תְּרוּמַת הַדֶּשֶׁן וְעֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה שְׁנֵי כְתוּבִין הַבָּאִין כְּאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the second example with one that works for every opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without בגדי כהונה, תרומת הדשן stands alone and should teach a general rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: עגלה ערופה is a second example, so the rule of two verses that teach the same law still applies.

steps.title: What about the view that two such verses do teach?
steps.stepSummary: The answer works for the view that two verses that teach the same law do not teach a rule. But some hold that they DO teach a rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the one who says two such verses do not teach a rule. But according to the one who says they do teach, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 15 using a known dispute. Some תנאים hold that two verses with the same law DO teach a general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 relied on the principle that two verses that teach the same law do not teach a rule. According to the other view, the two verses would teach that every item stays under מעילה after its מצוה. That would bring back the challenge against רב פפא's answer from Step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who says (a certain opinion)
They do teach a general rule
What can be said? (a formula for a challenge)

phrases.english: It works out well according to the one who said they do not teach
but according to the one who said they do teach
what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵין מְלַמְּדִין, אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מְלַמְּדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the principle that Step 15 relied on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of the principle that two verses that teach the same law do not teach a rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Some hold that two such verses DO teach a rule. For them, תרומת הדשן and עגלה ערופה would make every finished-מצוה item subject to מעילה.

steps.title: Each verse has a limiting word
steps.stepSummary: Each verse contains a word that limits it: ושמו ('it') and הערופה ('the one whose neck is broken'). So even the view that two verses do teach a rule cannot learn from these.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two limiting words are written. It says 'and he shall put it,' and it says 'the one whose neck is broken.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the תורה itself limits each law to its own case. This ends the side discussion about מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'it' in ושמו means only this item, the ashes. The word 'the' in הערופה means only this heifer. When the תורה writes such limiting words, no one generalizes from them, so רב פפא's answer in Step 10 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A word in the verse that limits or excludes
'And he shall put it,' said of the ashes
'The one whose neck is broken,' said of the heifer

steps.whatToRemember: An item whose מצוה is done generally has no מעילה. תרומת הדשן and עגלה ערופה are exceptions, limited by the words ושמו and הערופה, so no general rule is learned from them.

phrases.english: Two exclusions are written
it is written 'and he shall put it'
phrases.notes: 'It' means only this, the ashes.

phrases.english: and it is written 'the one whose neck was broken'
phrases.notes: 'The' means only this heifer.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּרֵי מִיעוּטֵי כְּתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 16 and closes the side discussion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to limiting words in the verses themselves
steps.terutzHavaAmina: According to the view that two verses do teach, these two would create a general rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each verse has a limiting word, so the law stays inside these two cases for everyone.

steps.title: A heifer that threshed grain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the dispute of אביי and רבא about benefit that cannot be avoided but is intended (לא אפשר ומתכוין). A ברייתא says a heifer that threshed without the owner's intent stays valid, but if he brought it in so it would nurse and also thresh, it is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If he brought the heifer into a stall and it threshed grain, it is valid. If he brought it in so that it would nurse and also thresh, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: With תא שמע, the גמרא leaves the side topic and brings a source for the main dispute of אביי and רבא. This step only presents the ברייתא; the גמרא will analyze it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A heifer used for work becomes unfit for its ritual. Here, threshing the owner did not intend leaves it valid. Threshing he did intend disqualifies it, even though the heifer had to go in to nurse anyway. The second case is לא אפשר ומתכוין, so the ruling supports רבא and challenges אביי, as the next step spells out.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a proof from a source)
A stall or pen for cattle
Valid, fit for the ritual
Disqualified, unfit for the ritual
So that it would nurse and thresh

steps.confusionAlert: The word רבקה here is not the name of the אמא. It means a cattle stall.
steps.whyThisMatters: It brings the sugya back to its main question: is a benefit permitted when it cannot be avoided but the person intends to enjoy it (לא אפשר ומתכוין)?

phrases.english: Come and hear
If one brought it into a stall and it threshed
it is valid
phrases.notes: He did not intend for it to work.

phrases.english: If he brought it in so that it would nurse and thresh
it is disqualified
phrases.notes: He intended the threshing as well.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הִכְנִיסָה לְרִבְקָה וְדָשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about מעילה and returns to the main dispute of אביי and רבא.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that לא אפשר ומתכוין is forbidden (against אביי)
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a heifer that threshed in a stall with or without the owner's intent

steps.title: The heifer case seems to prove that intended benefit is forbidden even when unavoidable
steps.stepSummary: In the heifer case the threshing could not be avoided, yet the owner wanted it, and the heifer is disqualified. So intended benefit is forbidden even when it cannot be avoided.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here is a case where it was not possible to avoid it, and he intended it, and the ברייתא teaches that the heifer is disqualified!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion from the ברייתא it quoted in step 18. Here the threshing could not be avoided and the owner wanted it, and still the heifer is disqualified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heifer had to go down to the barn to nurse, so the owner could not prevent the threshing. That makes this a case of 'not possible, but intended' (לא אפשר וקא מיכוין). The ruling of פסולה suggests that wanting the benefit is enough to forbid it, which challenges the view that permits such a case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not possible to avoid it. The act has no other way of happening.
He intends it. He wants the result or benefit.
Disqualified. Here, the heifer can no longer be used for the עגלה ערופה ritual.
And the source teaches. This introduces the ruling of the ברייתא as evidence.

steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate questions here. The first is whether the act could be avoided (אפשר or לא אפשר). The second is whether the person wanted the result (מיכוין or לא מיכוין). In this case the threshing could NOT be avoided, but the owner DID want it.

phrases.english: But here, isn't it a case where it was not possible to avoid it
phrases.notes: The heifer had to go down to the barn to nurse, and threshing happened along the way.

phrases.english: and he intended it,
phrases.notes: The owner wanted the heifer to thresh his grain.

phrases.english: and it teaches that it is disqualified!
phrases.notes: The גמרא is raising a challenge from this ruling.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הָכָא דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר וְקָא מִיכַּוֵּין, וְקָתָנֵי פְּסוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the ברייתא that was quoted in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's view that לא אפשר ומתכוין is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The heifer ruling forbids intended benefit even when it is unavoidable. That contradicts the permissive view.

steps.title: The heifer is different because its verse disqualifies any work
steps.stepSummary: The verse 'which has not been worked with' disqualifies the heifer in any case. So it is a special law and teaches no general rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because it is written: 'which has not been worked with', meaning in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. The heifer has its own special verse, so we cannot learn a general rule from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about עגלה ערופה says the animal must never have been worked. That disqualifies it whatever the reason the work happened. So the ruling comes from the heifer's own unique law, not from a general rule about intended benefit. The general dispute is left untouched.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there. This formula sets a source apart as a special case.
'Which has not been worked with' (דברים כא:ג). This is the requirement for the heifer.
In any case, no matter what. Any work at all disqualifies it.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common move in the גמרא. A ruling that rests on a special verse cannot be used to settle a general dispute.

phrases.english: It is different there, as it is written:
'Which has not been worked with', in any case.
phrases.notes: The verse is read as disqualifying the heifer for any work, whatever the circumstances.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 19 by limiting the heifer ruling to its own verse.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the heifer case as proof in the general dispute about intended benefit.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The heifer is disqualified by a special verse that rules out any work at all, so its ruling is not based on intent.

steps.title: If any work disqualifies, the first case should also be disqualified
steps.stepSummary: If the verse disqualifies any work, then even unintended threshing should disqualify the heifer. Yet the first part of the ברייתא says it stays valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then even in the first clause it should also be disqualified!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If any work disqualifies, the first part of the ברייתא makes no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause (רישא) said that if the heifer threshed without the owner's intent, it stays valid. But if the verse means 'any work at all', unintended threshing is still work and should disqualify it. So the 'in any case' reading seems to contradict the ברייתא itself.

keyTerms.meaning: If so. This introduces a problem that follows from the answer just given.
The first clause of the source. Here, the case where the heifer threshed without the owner's intent.
Also, too.

phrases.english: If so, even the first clause too!
phrases.notes: Even the first clause should then rule the heifer disqualified.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי אֲפִילּוּ רֵישָׁא נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rejection given in step 20 by checking it against the first clause of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of 'אשר לא עבד בה' as meaning 'in any case' (step 20).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If any work disqualifies, then unintended threshing should also disqualify. But the רישא rules that the heifer stays valid.
